question: Inserting a grommet (ventilation tube) to treat autophony caused by a patulous Eustachian tube will worsen the patient's symptoms.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. This statement is true and represents a critical trap. In patulous ET, the ET is already too open. A grommet equalises middle ear pressure with the environment, removing any remaining resistance and worsening autophony. Grommets are contraindicated in patulous ET.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. In patulous ET, the tube is pathologically open — the patient hears their own breath and voice (autophony) because the normally closed tube transmits nasopharyngeal pressure directly to the middle ear. A grommet equalises middle ear pressure with the external ear canal, thereby bypassing the ET entirely and preventing any natural pressure build-up that might reduce autophony. Many patients report that the grommet makes their autophony significantly worse. The correct management is conservative (saline nasal drops, weight gain if underweight) or surgical narrowing of the ET.
